results.title: Christmas Games For Teens Printable | Phone Round, Gift Swap Game, Lip Read and 60 Dares and Forfeits PDF
results.description:
A Christmas night built for teenagers, which means it is neither a children's party nor an adults' one.

That is the whole problem with every other pack. One has a cartoon snowman on it and a fifteen year old will not touch it. The other has drinking in it and you cannot hand it to a room of them. Both get rejected in about four seconds.

So this is four games that work at that age, plus the structure to run them.

THE PHONE ROUND is the thing every other pack bans. Twenty challenges answered straight off the phone in their pocket: lowest battery, most unread notifications, oldest photo on the camera roll, the longest group chat name anybody is in, a screenshot you cannot explain. It is the fastest warm up there is, and it buys you the right to say phones down for the rest of the night.

THE SWAP is a gift game run by forty action cards instead of by an adult. Open it now. Pass two places left. Steal an opened one. Immunity, nobody can take yours. The cards make every decision, which is exactly why it works where a normal gift swap turns into an argument by the fourth turn, because nobody has to be the person who took a present off somebody.

LIP READ is one person mouthing a phrase with no sound while their team tries to say it back word for word. Forty eight of them, and not one is a film, song or television title, because an ordinary sentence like I think the dog ate it is far funnier to watch somebody mouth than any title.

THEN THE DARES AND FORFEITS. Thirty six dares and twenty four forfeits, and whoever comes last picks their own forfeit before anybody picks it for them. That one rule is what stops these evenings ending early.

What you get:
. The Phone Round, twenty challenges
. The Swap, the rules and forty action cards
. Lip Read, the rules and forty eight phrase cards
. The Dares Deck, thirty six cards
. The Forfeits Deck, twenty four cards
. Forty quiz questions over two rounds, with the full answer key
. A running order, two hours and ten minutes
. The Six Rules, read out before anything starts
. If It Goes Quiet, eight rescues for when it stalls
. A scorecard for six players and two certificates
. Every page in two sizes, US Letter and A4

A word on what is NOT in it, because this is the part parents ask about. No alcohol. Nothing sexual. Nothing about anybody's body, appearance or who they like. No dare that involves going outside alone, heights, eating anything, or touching anybody else's phone. Nothing gets posted, sent or shown outside the room. And PASS is printed as rule one: anybody can pass on anything, without explaining, without losing a point.

Who is it for? Thirteen to eighteen. Youth groups, sleepovers, sixth form and school parties, and the house where the teenagers have ended up on the twenty seventh and nobody knows what to do with them.
